standard_prerequisites: formal spectra of adic Noetherian rings and morphisms given by continuous ring maps
rig-surjectivity tested by lifts along adic maps to complete discrete valuation rings
the completed base change C = B completed tensor_A R and its reduction properties
going-down for flat maps and the Jacobson complement-of-a-closed-point lemma
existence of a one-dimensional local domain quotient embedding into a discrete valuation ring
core_obligations: Prove that if A is I-adically complete Noetherian, B is I-adically complete over A, the reductions A/I^n to B/I^nB are finite type and flat for all n and faithfully flat for n = 1, then Spf(B) to Spf(A) is rig-surjective
proof_roadmap: Test rig-surjectivity on a continuous map A to R into a complete discrete valuation ring with phi(I) contained in the maximal ideal; for adic test maps phi(I) is nonzero
Form the completed base change C = B completed tensor over A with R; its reductions over R/m^n are finite type flat and C/mC is nonzero by faithful flatness in degree one

Pick a maximal ideal m of C over m_R; by going-down the complement of V(m_R C_m) in Spec(C_m) is nonempty, and the Jacobson lemma supplies a prime q inside m defining a closed point of that complement outside V(I C_m)

The quotient C/q is a one-dimensional local domain, which embeds into a discrete valuation ring R' containing R; the map C to R' is continuous and extends to the completion, producing the commutative square that gives the lift B' to R'
difficulty_reason: H2: a lift-construction argument through a base change, a dimension-one quotient and a DVR embedding; each step is written out with its quoted lemma.
